title: Dumpster Rental Software: 6 Tools for Dispatch, Billing and Leads
html:
Dumpster rental software starts with dispatch, billing and a lead source. Roll-off specific platforms such as Docket run the dispatch board and driver app, while Jobber and Housecall Pro suit a smaller fleet. Pair one of them with QuickBooks for the books and a free Google Business Profile for local calls. Published plans run from $12 to $299 a month, and Docket does not publish a price.

Dumpster rental software has to answer one question all day: where is every container and who owes money on it? A yard with a dozen roll-offs can track that on paper. A yard with forty cannot. This guide sorts six tools by the job they do, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Dumpster rental is a logistics trade. A customer books a drop, the container sits for days, a driver swaps or hauls it, and the invoice depends on the dump weight and the days out. Generic field service apps handle part of that. Roll-off platforms handle more of it.

Which dumpster rental software handles dispatch and driver routes?

Docket is the roll-off specific option here, and Jobber and Housecall Pro are the general field service options. All three schedule work and assign it to a person in the field.

  • Docket: built for roll-off and dumpster haulers. Its site describes one dispatch board for deliveries, swaps and removals, a driver app that works online and offline, asset tracking and billing tied to field activity. Plans are Grow, Pro and Pro Plus, billed monthly per truck, and office staff are free. Limit: prices are not published, and the vendor states a one-year agreement.
  • Jobber: a general field service app with scheduling, quotes, invoices and online payments. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Limit: extra users cost $29 a month each, and its published plans does not list container tracking.
  • Housecall Pro: scheduling, dispatch, estimates and invoices in one app. Basic is $59 a month billed annually for one user, or $79 billed monthly. Limit: add-ons such as payroll and websites are listed without prices.

The real question is whether you track containers or only jobs. A general app tracks the job. It will not tell you that container 14 has sat at a customer site for nine days. If idle containers cost you money, ask each vendor to show asset tracking in a live demo before you pay anything.

Route changes are the second test. A driver who gets a new swap at 2 p.m. should see it on the phone without a call to the office. Docket says a job moved to another driver updates the driver app, and that is the kind of claim to verify in a trial. Jobber offers a 14 day trial with no credit card, which lets you test a schedule with your own addresses.

What software handles dumpster rental billing and invoices?

QuickBooks handles the books and Joist handles fast invoices and estimates. A dumpster invoice is rarely a flat fee, so check how each tool prices a base rental plus extra days and overweight charges.

  • QuickBooks: accounting, invoicing and bank feeds. Simple Start is $38 a month, Essentials is $85 and Plus is $140, with promotional prices for the first three months. Limit: the free tier allows 2 invoices a month and 1 bank connection, and the page lists no price for extra users.
  • Joist: estimates, invoices and online payments for small contractors. Basics is $12 a month billed monthly, Pro is $17 and Elite is $32. Limit: Basics caps you at 5 documents a month, and the free plan is no longer offered.

Card fees matter more than the plan price in a rental business. Docket lists 3.0% plus 30 cents on Grow and 2.8% plus 30 cents on Pro and Pro Plus, with ACH at 1%. Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents for cards and 1% for bank payments. A $400 rental on a 3% fee costs you about $12 before the plan price.

ToolJob it doesPublished priceReal limit
DocketDispatch, driver app, billingNot published, per truckOne-year agreement
JobberScheduling, quotes, invoices$49 monthly, $29 annual (1 user)$29 per extra user
Housecall ProDispatch, estimates, invoices$59 annual, $79 monthly (1 user)Add-ons unpriced
QuickBooksAccounting$38 to $140 a monthPromo ends after 3 months
JoistFast invoices$12 to $32 a month5 documents on Basics
Google Business ProfileLocal listingFree to createNeeds steady upkeep

Prices checked on each vendor page in November 2026. Annual prices are per month billed yearly.

How do dumpster rental companies bring in leads?

Most dumpster customers search on a phone, name a city and call the first company that looks open. That makes the map listing the first lead tool to set up.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your yard, service area, photos, reviews and phone number in Google Search and Maps. Google states that creating a profile and listing your business is free. Limit: it only works if your hours, service area and photos stay current, and Google's paid ad products are separate.

Photos of real containers at real driveways do more than stock images. Reviews that mention same-day delivery help too.

Software tracks the order, but it does not create the search. Rankings from dumpster rental SEO and paid clicks from dumpster rental Google Ads send callers to your phone.

What does one dumpster rental look like from booking to invoice?

One rental touches every tool in the stack, so walk a single order through it before you buy. This is the path to test in any demo.

  • Call or booking: the customer finds your listing, calls and gives an address, container size and drop date.
  • Scheduling: the office enters the order and assigns a driver and a time window.
  • Delivery: the driver drops the container, takes a photo of the placement and marks the stop complete.
  • Swap or pickup: the customer calls to swap, and the office moves the job to the next open route.
  • Invoice: the rental days, extra days and any overweight charge become one invoice sent by text or email.
  • Payment and review: the customer pays by card or bank transfer, and you ask for a review while the job is fresh.

Every step that still happens on a sticky note is a place to lose money. If a tool cannot carry an order through all six steps without retyping, keep looking or plan for a second tool to fill the gap.

What does a dumpster rental software stack cost for a small yard?

A small yard with two trucks can budget between $12 and a few hundred dollars a month for software, depending on how much it automates. The range below uses only published prices.

  • Lean start: Joist Basics at $12 a month, a free Google Business Profile and a spreadsheet for container locations. Cost: $12 a month plus card fees.
  • Middle setup: Jobber Core at $49 a month month to month, QuickBooks Simple Start at $38 and a free Google Business Profile. Cost: $87 a month before extra users and card fees.
  • Roll-off platform: Docket per truck with QuickBooks for the books. Docket does not publish a price, so request a quote for your truck count and ask what onboarding costs.

The lean start is a starting point, not a finished system. A spreadsheet fails when two people edit it at once. Move to a real dispatch tool the week a driver goes to the wrong address because the sheet was out of date.

What should you ask a dumpster rental software vendor before signing?

Ask for answers in writing, because the demo and the contract can differ. Six questions cover most of the risk for a yard that rents roll-offs.

  • What is the term? Docket states a one-year agreement. Jobber lists monthly, one-year and annual pricing, so you can start month to month and move to a yearly plan later.
  • How is the price counted? Per truck, per user or per job changes your bill as you grow. A yard that adds seasonal drivers should model the busy month, not the slow one.
  • What are the card and bank fees? Get the rate for credit cards and for bank transfers. Large commercial customers can often pay by bank transfer at a lower fee.
  • Can drivers work without signal? Many yards sit in places with weak coverage. Docket says its driver app works online and offline, so test any app you consider in your worst dead zone.
  • What happens to your data if you leave? Ask how you export customers, containers and invoices. A tool you cannot leave becomes a bigger cost than its plan price.
  • Does it connect to your accounting? Double entry between a dispatch tool and QuickBooks wastes hours every week. Ask which integrations are included in your plan and which cost extra.

Pilot the tool on one route for a week. Count how many calls to the office disappear, how many invoices go out on the day the container is picked up, and how many containers you can find without phoning a driver. Those three numbers tell you more than any feature list.

Do not skip training. A dispatch board only helps when every driver updates a stop on the spot. Pick the person who will own the tool, give that person a day to load customers and containers, and decide in advance who corrects bad data. Yards that skip this step often blame the software for a process problem.

How do you choose dumpster rental software?

Choose dumpster rental software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you sign a contract.

Fit: does it track each container, assign swaps to drivers and bill by day or by weight?

Cost: add the plan, per truck or per user charges, card fees and any add-ons, then compare against one average rental.

Setup effort: can you load your customers and containers in a weekend, and will your drivers use the app?

A one or two truck yard fits Jobber or Housecall Pro with QuickBooks. A growing fleet that runs several swaps a day fits a roll-off platform like Docket better. Whichever you pick, run a trial week with your real routes before you commit to a yearly term.

What software does a dumpster rental company need?

A dumpster rental company needs dispatch for drivers, billing for rentals and a lead source such as a Google Business Profile. Start with a scheduling and invoicing tool, then add roll-off asset tracking once you run enough containers that locations get lost or idle days go unbilled.

How much does dumpster rental software cost?

Published plans in this guide run from $12 a month for Joist Basics to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max, billed annually. Docket does not publish prices and bills per truck. Card fees, extra users and add-ons cost more, so ask each vendor for a full quote.

Is Docket software worth it for a small dumpster yard?

It can be if you track many containers and run swaps daily, because it is built for roll-offs. Docket bills monthly per truck and its published plans states a one-year agreement. A yard with one or two trucks should run a demo and compare the total against Jobber.

Can Jobber or Housecall Pro run a dumpster rental business?

Both handle scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so they can run the jobs side. Neither is built around container tracking. Jobber lists a one-user plan at $49 a month with no commitment, and Housecall Pro lists one user at $59 a month billed annually.

Is Google Business Profile free for dumpster rental companies?

Google states that creating a Business Profile and listing your business on Google is free. You still need to add photos, set a service area and reply to reviews. Google paid ad products are separate, and managed help costs extra.

Should a dumpster rental company use QuickBooks too?

Many do, because dispatch tools focus on jobs and QuickBooks focuses on the books. Simple Start is listed at $38 a month and Plus at $140, with promotional prices for the first three months. Check what each dispatch tool syncs before you pay for both.

How do dumpster rental companies get more phone calls?

Most calls come from local search, so a complete Google Business Profile, a fast mobile site and reviews matter first. Paid search can fill gaps. Software then makes sure each call becomes a booked drop and an invoice instead of a missed message.

Docket states a one-year agreement. Jobber lists monthly, one-year and annual pricing, so you can start month to month and move to a yearly plan later.
-
How is the price counted?
Per truck, per user or per job changes your bill as you grow. A yard that adds seasonal drivers should model the busy month, not the slow one.
-
What are the card and bank fees?
Get the rate for credit cards and for bank transfers. Large commercial customers can often pay by bank transfer at a lower fee.
-
Can drivers work without signal?
Many yards sit in places with weak coverage. Docket says its driver app works online and offline, so test any app you consider in your worst dead zone.
-
What happens to your data if you leave?
Ask how you export customers, containers and invoices. A tool you cannot leave becomes a bigger cost than its plan price.
-
Does it connect to your accounting?
Double entry between a dispatch tool and QuickBooks wastes hours every week. Ask which integrations are included in your plan and which cost extra.
Pilot the tool on one route for a week. Count how many calls to the office disappear, how many invoices go out on the day the container is picked up, and how many containers you can find without phoning a driver. Those three numbers tell you more than any feature list.
Do not skip training. A dispatch board only helps when every driver updates a stop on the spot. Pick the person who will own the tool, give that person a day to load customers and containers, and decide in advance who corrects bad data. Yards that skip this step often blame the software for a process problem.
##
How do you choose dumpster rental software?
Choose dumpster rental software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you sign a contract.
Fit:
does it track each container, assign swaps to drivers and bill by day or by weight?
Cost:
add the plan, per truck or per user charges, card fees and any add-ons, then compare against one average rental.
Setup effort:
can you load your customers and containers in a weekend, and will your drivers use the app?
A one or two truck yard fits Jobber or Housecall Pro with QuickBooks. A growing fleet that runs several swaps a day fits a roll-off platform like Docket better. Whichever you pick, run a trial week with your real routes before you commit to a yearly term.
###
What software does a dumpster rental company need?
A dumpster rental company needs dispatch for drivers, billing for rentals and a lead source such as a Google Business Profile. Start with a scheduling and invoicing tool, then add roll-off asset tracking once you run enough containers that locations get lost or idle days go unbilled.
###
How much does dumpster rental software cost?
Published plans in this guide run from $12 a month for Joist Basics to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max, billed annually. Docket does not publish prices and bills per truck. Card fees, extra users and add-ons cost more, so ask each vendor for a full quote.
###
Is Docket software worth it for a small dumpster yard?
It can be if you track many containers and run swaps daily, because it is built for roll-offs. Docket bills monthly per truck and its published plans states a one-year agreement. A yard with one or two trucks should run a demo and compare the total against Jobber.
###
Can Jobber or Housecall Pro run a dumpster rental business?
Both handle scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so they can run the jobs side. Neither is built around container tracking. Jobber lists a one-user plan at $49 a month with no commitment, and Housecall Pro lists one user at $59 a month billed annually.
###
Is Google Business Profile free for dumpster rental companies?
Google states that creating a Business Profile and listing your business on Google is free. You still need to add photos, set a service area and reply to reviews. Google paid ad products are separate, and managed help costs extra.
###
Should a dumpster rental company use QuickBooks too?
Many do, because dispatch tools focus on jobs and QuickBooks focuses on the books. Simple Start is listed at $38 a month and Plus at $140, with promotional prices for the first three months. Check what each dispatch tool syncs before you pay for both.
###
How do dumpster rental companies get more phone calls?
Most calls come from local search, so a complete Google Business Profile, a fast mobile site and reviews matter first. Paid search can fill gaps. Software then makes sure each call becomes a booked drop and an invoice instead of a missed message.
